solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boycott is no way to face discrimination

parts.note: O is a nought, a zero or no amount
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
racism is discrimination on grounds of race

explanation.surface: A campaigner argues that refusing to deal with someone is no way to confront prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to face' just sets the pieces side by side, the street abbreviation facing (coming before) the word for prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott is to shun or exclude, and exclusion from society is the classic sense of the noun.

clue.text: For example, Julius Caesar's works in Latin

definitions.meaning: Handel's Giulio Cesare is a stage work set to music, so Julius Caesar is an example of one
the Latin plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar's writings, such as the Gallic Wars, were composed in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Caesar the author; the first sense is Handel's musical drama named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical drama sung on stage is the genre, and Latin for several works is the plural of opus.

clue.text: I'm happier now I recognise St Thomas: say so on Facebook?

parts.note: spotting Sir Thomas More, the saint, you might say 'that's More'
clicking the thumbs-up button on Facebook is to 'like' a post

explanation.surface: Someone spots a picture of St Thomas and wonders whether to give it a thumbs-up online.
explanation.walkthrough: St Thomas is Sir Thomas More, the Tudor chancellor later canonised.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of approval, said when things improve to one's satisfaction.

clue.text: Skilful composer makes records

parts.note: arch means cunning or crafty, skilful in a sly way
Charles Ives was an American composer

explanation.surface: A talented composer produces recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'records' looks like discs a composer makes; it is the noun for stored documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents, that is, stored records.

clue.text: Cheeky fellow, one in African force

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous, cheeky child
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cheeky chap serves as a member of an African army.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a Zulu regiment, an armed body of warriors in southern Africa.

clue.text: A team of Scots make good parents

definitions.meaning: ... FC plays in the Scottish football league
to bring up children well, read as two words: rear them in a fine manner

explanation.surface: A claim that Scottish people turn out to be fine mothers and fathers.
explanation.walkthrough: Motherwell is a town near Glasgow whose football club plays in the Scottish league; split in two the name tells you to raise children properly.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club is a Scottish side, and the split phrase means to raise offspring properly.

clue.text: Panic, grabbed by fanatical army

indicators.note: the letters are seized inside the words fanatical army, held across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Fear sweeps through as a zealous army seizes control.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxiety, a synonym for panic.

clue.text: "Riding a pig" day

parts.note: a boar is a male or wild pig

explanation.surface: Reads like a headline about a day of pig-riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone riding on a train or ship is on board, carried as a passenger.

clue.text: Suggesting no actor involved in this?

definitions.text: Suggesting no actor involved in this?

parts.words: Suggesting no actor involved in this?
parts.note: a drawn film needs no live performer; and the second word is the letters of no actor, while the first word can signal a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A question about a film in which no actor takes part.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: drawn films have no live actors, and the answer itself 'suggests' NO ACTOR, its second word being those letters shuffled, its first word a typical anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn or computer-made film has characters voiced but not acted on screen.

clue.text: Unique, unlike Andersen's little girl

definitions.meaning: Hans Christian Andersen's Little Match Girl carried matches; unlike her means having none

explanation.surface: One-of-a-kind, unlike the girl in Andersen's fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal or rival is unique, and read literally the word means lacking lights for a fire.

clue.text: Freedom-fighter's actions inept — I am worried

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel leader frets that their deeds have been clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' shuffles ACTIONS INEPT I AM; the 's after the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who campaigns to free slaves or the oppressed is a liberator, a fighter for freedom.

clue.text: Muscles relax, about to let oneself down

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word for relax round

parts.note: to lie is to rest, relax

explanation.surface: Someone loosens up their muscles before going down a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like low spirits, but 'let oneself down' here is literal: descending a cliff on a rope. 'about' reverses the word for relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling is descending a rock face on a rope, literally lowering yourself.

clue.text: Preach, or otherwise censure

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to deliver a sermon or else criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach is to rebuke or express disapproval, the same as censure.

clue.text: Notice sister working with no finesse

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a notice

indicators.note: working means in motion or being reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An advert for a sister's job that requires no delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' shuffles SISTER and NO into ROITNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is skill and delicacy in handling something, which is what dexterity or deftness means.

clue.text: Analysed range of perception dog nearly had in colour

indicators.note: the colour has the other pieces put inside it

parts.note: brown is a colour
ken is one's range of knowledge or sight

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of the word dog, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A dog's field of vision analysed in terms of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface leans on the idea that dogs see few colours. 'nearly' docks the dog's tail letter, and 'had in' sets the knowledge word plus that remnant inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure broken down into parts has been analysed, separated into components.

clue.text: Tour show in pubs across the north — decline to go up motorway

indicators.note: the pubs stretch across, enclosing, the north

parts.note: bars are pubs
N is the abbreviation for north

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: rot is decay, decline
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A touring show plays pubs across the north, then refuses to head up the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts N in BARS; 'to go up' turns ROT into TOR. 'decline' in the surface means refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To barnstorm is to tour rural areas putting on shows, originally in barns.

clue.text: Poet's dry, but sounds visionary

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is matched by how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: a seer is a prophet, a visionary

explanation.surface: A poet is dry, yet sounds like a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere is an archaic, literary word for withered or parched, used chiefly in verse.

clue.text: Easier way to get a number one?

definitions.meaning: a quicker route than the usual one
a number one is the closest clipper setting, giving very cropped hair

explanation.surface: Asks for a quick route to the top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'number one' in Britain is a very close haircut made with the shortest clipper guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A quicker route is a time-saving path, and a cropped haircut is a brief trim.

clue.text: Stink in river that's frightening

parts.note: eek is an exclamation of fright

explanation.surface: A bad smell in a river is alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to give off a strong unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Entirely unopened, white wines which may be placed in bed

definitions.text: which may be placed in bed

indicators.note: unopened means without its first letter

parts.note: wholly means entirely
hock is German white wine, from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Bottles of white wine taken to bed without being opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not one you sleep in.
explanation.definitionFit: These tall garden flowers are planted in a flower bed.

clue.text: Pulse, that is, one on the head

parts.note: a bean is a pulse, an edible seed
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A doctor takes a pulse, then examines a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting woollen hat is worn on the head.

clue.text: Told to go round capturing Ice Age in painting

indicators.note: the first word captures, encloses, the second

parts.note: someone told to go is sent away
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Instructions to circle a painting of the Ice Age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice Age' reads as one phrase, but only the first word is wordplay; 'Age in painting' is the definition, an Italian art-history term. 'capturing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The seicento is the 17th century in Italian art, an era of painting.

clue.text: Diagnostician perhaps right person to see about infestation

parts.note: DR, doctor, is an example of one who diagnoses

indicators.note: about turns the word for right person round

parts.note: a Tory is a right-wing person

explanation.surface: A specialist is called to look into a pest problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TORY into YROT.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal decay of timber is an infestation of wood by fungus.

clue.text: Hear hard men are thrown out of short meeting

parts.note: a judge hears, tries, a case

indicators.note: the letters are expelled from the word short

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
OR, other ranks, means men in the army

explanation.surface: Tough guys ejected from a brief meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are thrown out of' removes H and OR from SHORT, leaving ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a romantic rendezvous, an arranged meeting.

clue.text: Young trumpeter's signal that's short and loud

indicators.note: short means lacking its final letter

parts.note: a bugle call is a trumpeter's signal
F is forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: A young trumpeter plays a short, loud signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last L of CALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A calf is the young of a cow, so young here is a noun for offspring.

clue.text: In theatre, compere retains vigour to introduce sacred verse

parts.note: Odeon is a chain of cinemas, a picture theatre

indicators.note: the compere's letters hold the word for vigour inside

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a compere
élan is vigour, dash
holy means sacred

explanation.surface: At a theatre, the host keeps up energy before a religious poem is read.
explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is a British cinema chain, a familiar crossword 'theatre'. 'retains' signals the container; 'sacred verse' looks like one phrase but only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Keats's 1819 poem, a famous piece of verse.

clue.text: Rhythm is just keeping time

parts.note: mere means only, just

explanation.surface: Rhythm is simply a matter of keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts T inside MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the rhythmic pattern of verse, its measured beat.

clue.text: One stops diver unintentionally moving fast with energy across river

indicators.note: the shuffled letters stretch across the others
moving means set in motion, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
the Tyne is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A daredevil diver racing across a river in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'unintentional diver' is someone who falls. 'moving' shuffles the fast letters, and 'across' wraps them round energy and the river of Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh under acrobats catches anyone who falls, stopping an accidental plunge.
